title: A Promised Son for Manoah's Wife
overview: While Israel suffers under the Philistines, a mysterious messenger promises a childless couple a son, Samson, who will be set apart for God and begin Israel's rescue.

parts.label: Under Philistine rule (v. 1)
parts.note: The book's familiar cycle starts again: Israel turns away from the LORD and falls under a foreign power. The Philistines were a strong people on the coastal plain, and at forty years this is the longest oppression in the book.

parts.label: A promise to a childless woman (vv. 2-5)
parts.note: Zorah was a town of the tribe of Dan near the Philistine border, and being childless was a deep grief and often a social shame then. Her son is to be a Nazirite, someone set apart for God who drinks no wine and never cuts his hair, so she must keep the same food rules because his dedication begins in the womb.

parts.label: Manoah asks for more (vv. 6-14)
parts.note: The unnamed wife tells her husband everything, and Manoah prays for the visitor to return and teach them how to raise the boy. When he comes back, he points Manoah to what he already told her and adds that she must avoid anything that comes from the grapevine.

parts.label: A meal becomes an offering (vv. 15-20)
parts.note: Manoah offers a guest meal, but the visitor refuses to eat, tells him to make it an offering to the LORD, and won't give his name because it is 'wonderful' or beyond understanding. He then rises up in the altar's flame, and many Christians have read this figure as Christ appearing before his birth, though the passage itself does not say so.

parts.label: Fear and a sensible answer (vv. 21-23)
parts.note: An old belief held that seeing God directly meant death, so Manoah panics. His wife reasons calmly that the LORD would not accept their offering and make them promises only to kill them.

parts.label: Samson is born (vv. 24-25)
parts.note: The name Samson probably relates to the Hebrew word for sun, though scholars are unsure of its exact sense. As he grows, the Spirit of the LORD begins to stir him at Mahaneh Dan, meaning 'Camp of Dan', near his home town.

disagreement: Christians differ on who 'the angel of the LORD' is here: some see a created angel speaking for God, while others see God himself appearing, often understood as Christ before his birth.
think: Manoah panics while his wife reasons calmly from what has actually happened; when something overwhelming happens to you, which way do you tend to lean?
